# 1.2.112 - the dead as Spectators, the table's dice look, the player and GM screens' cleanup, tooltips across the module, the action grid in the owner's order, the curtain under the windows, every field of the case planner, and the second security round's tests

One train on 1.2.111 (984d1fb1, and main's a31e7a3b with 1.2.111's test fix, merged in 292a0f48). One stage of the
ledger ships here: E108 (the table's dice look, Dice So Nice's or Daggerheart's), with the DH212b line it sits on.
Beside it, the lines merged into the 1.2.112 tree, in this order: r112 (E100 and E101b, the player and GM screens;
3fef1b2f), E102 (tooltips; 472e1ea0), the e72 line to 72c384d8 (E62 C3b, the dead as Spectators, and E106, the Monocub's
token; 3b0d8075), E103 (the action tiles; 2c982c21), E105 (the curtain under the windows; 5fe34890), E107 (a GM's tile
wears the chip; 27801820), gaps-111 (1.2.105's known gaps and the late sequence; 12090776), E39 and E40's C1 (the e39-40
line to ad4499a4; f26044e8), E43 (the second security round, to e52ce98e; 28f131aa), E104 (the case planner plans every
field, the e97-98 line to c3224b42; 583f95b4) and the dh-212b line (E108 and DH212b, abe0972f; 9a735dd6). From a31e7a3b
to 8834a9b9, the tree before its release commit: one hundred and ninety-eight commits, twenty-three of them merges (`git
rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over a31e7a3b..8834a9b9), eighteen on the tree itself (`--first-parent`).

**This release did not run the full test gate, by the owner's choice (13.11.2026).** Before this commit only the quick
gate ran (lint, every check part, the gate's self-test, the Polish prose) and, once, tiers 0-1 headless; CI's whole
suite, its scenarios and the local gate did not. release.yml runs CI on this commit before it builds anything.

E102, E39, E40 and E43 are in the tree but stay open in tools/stages.json (below, Known gaps): E102 has its C6 still to
do, E40 its C2-C4 (for 1.2.114), E39's fourteen FLOWS rows still name it as the stage that covers them, and E43's own
release steps (its LIVE rows, the README chapter) are the owner's to take.

In plain words:

**E108, the table's dice look.** The game's settings (Rolls and privacy) held one switch, "force Dice So Nice's look".
It is now one choice of three, **Dice look for the table** / **Wygląd kości przy stole**: **Each player's own** (as
the switch off), **Everyone: Dice So Nice** (as the switch on) and **Everyone: Daggerheart**. With Daggerheart chosen,
the Hope, Fear, advantage and disadvantage dice wear Daggerheart's own colours on every screen, whoever throws, a GM
too; the basic dice keep the GM's Dice So Nice look (Daggerheart has none for them). Only the dice's look changes, never
the roll. The forced look now carries the source GM's Dice So Nice role looks as well (Q-E108-2, the coordinator's
default "yes"; the line had marked it for 1.2.113, and it came with the line's tip). Without Dice So Nice there are no
3D dice whatever the choice.

**DH212b, Daggerheart 2.12.8's dice road** (the line E108 sits on): a GM's pick card and a player's payment are taken
the moment they land, not at the next tenth of a second; a player whose drawn roll's dice have not started 600 ms
after it was asked is told "The GM is throwing your dice." (600 ms is chosen, not measured); a drawn roll asked
again once a GM is ready is answered from the GM's record instead of judged afresh; a GM's Reroll reads the roll's
effects as Daggerheart 2.10 and 2.12 keep them.

**E100, the player screens** (the player-screens review the owner approved on 12.11.2026; items 2 and 5 reverted at
the owner's word, so the settings window, the Sound window and Search's statistic are as in 1.2.108):
- **Move opens no window**: a student drags the token. A Monocub's panel says "Free" under its tiles while its next
  crossing is free.
- **The verbose console** is a GM's switch alone; a player's settings window has no Technical section.
- **The notice history's filters**: All, For you, Not done as chips; the rest in one "More filters" list, each with
  its count.
- **One word per kind of button**: rolls "Roll" / "Rzuć", the GM decides "Send to the GM" / "Wyślij do GM-a", a step
  that leads on "Next" / "Dalej"; Rest's picks "Rest" / "Odpocznij"; an open Frisk "Ask them" / "Poproś".
- **The explainers** count the shown character's own actions.
- **No fold in an action window**: "Rolls: <statistic>" stands in the window's lead after the description.
- **The sheet's Stop** shows the table's word alone; the sheet's left column no longer scrolls sideways; the chosen
  tab is marked again.
- **The GM's status strip stands in a Class Trial** again.

**E101 (with E101b), the GM screens** (the owner's yes of 12.11.2026 to the GM screens' review):
- **Season setup** holds Edit campaign's next morning's line, the Scenes part that was Room setup's tab, and Reset
  the season in a warning frame at its foot, out of the footer; its tiles open their windows without closing it.
- **The Season checklist and Pre-season checks** are one window; the checks a GM cannot act on before a session went to
  the Debug log's "Foundry and modules" button.
- **Despair Flow** with one pool holder opens on Overflow; the Monokumas tab lists Monokumas alone.
- **Room setup**: one line over the tabs says what Apply saves; the first tab is Rooms (this is a room, whose
  bedroom, no privacy); Doors holds the locks, Broken and the neighbours; no Scenes tab.
- **The game's settings**: the Music and Vary the sounds switches are the Sound window's; Foundry's own switches under
  "Foundry and the system"; "GM tools and map" is "Map"; the window keeps one size from section to section.
- **The GM panel**: the students line is the count alone (the Now section's Students tile is the door); the clock and
  Next time of day centred on two rows.
- **Give / take items**: one Give tab asking what and from where; **Level Up** in one window with Grant; the item
  tables' Tier pools without New or Rename.
- **Smaller**: Interface scale's field reads 0.95, not 0.9500000000000001; the microphone's two modes are buttons; the
  Class Trial console's row of modes wraps instead of scrolling; Sound and Music in one column.
- **Fixes from the r112 review**: Despair Flow's Save keeps the pool of a Monokuma made while it stood open; Move's
  words hold where Move does (not in a Class Trial or an incident the character is in); the checklist raises Season
  setup over itself; the texts that sent a GM to Room setup's Scenes tab name Season setup.
- **A secret project's countdown tells no player apart** (S17-31's follow-up, R4620, R4621): every player of the world
  one level in its map, and the reseal at load waits for the GMs' copies.

**E102, tooltips across the module** (the owner's stage of 13.11.2026; not finished, so not shipped): the actions'
and projects' windows, the chapter, murder and Class Trial windows, the GM panels, the setup windows and the sheet
draw tooltips from one new block of keys (`DRPG.Tips`), in English and Polish, at most 23 words each; 171 keys after
this tree's merges.
A tooltip is written only when it has words. `node tools/check.mjs tooltips` holds every control drawn with neither a
tooltip nor a hint line to tools/tooltip-census.json, which may only shrink. C6 (the Investigation and the case) is
still to do. Merged into this tree after main had moved on, the 1.2.110-1.2.112 code drew 73 controls the census had
not seen (74 at the merges, one since given a hint); each is a row "E102 C12: ..." in the census, to be given its tooltip or a reason before E102 ships (below).

**E62 C3b, the dead as Spectators** (the owner's "E62 c3b wszystko sie zgadza", 13.11.2026): when a student dies and is
no Monocub, a GM's browser makes their player a Spectator of their own - a new character with the student's name,
portrait and token picture, owned by that player alone - and a token where the body lies; the body's token stays the
corpse. The player moves it anywhere, free; other players do not see it, the GM sees it faint. The dead still see only
what a dead student sees. A Monocub takes the Spectator's token as its own, where it stands; the Spectator goes, the
corpse stays. A revive and the season reset take the Spectator away. The silenced dead talk in the Spectators' room.
The Students window shows a dead student's Spectator's Role as words. On the dead player's own screen the curtain
plays the death fade (3.6 s) and, for a Monocub, its return; the rest state is bare glass. A new Sound row, "Death
fade" / "Gaśnięcie".

**E106, the Monocub's token**: the Spectator's (and so the Monocub's) token wears the body's token's look - its
picture's scale and fit, its size, its ring - where it came back smaller; and the body tile's mark takes no click, so a
double-click on a Monocub standing on its own body opens its sheet.

**E103, the action tiles** (the owner's decision of 13.11.2026): the student's grid in the owner's order - Search,
Observe, Analyze, Infiltrate, Palm, then Projects, Facilities, Dynamic, Tamper, Direct Murder (the last two's order a
default, the owner to confirm). A Monocub has no Move tile; its two feet in the sheet's header and on its strip always
read as available ("A Monocub moves freely ..."), in an Eclipse too.

**E105, the curtain under the windows** (the owner's ask of 13.11.2026): at the Class Trial's entry and exit the closing
curtain is drawn under the open windows, and the title with its band and the chapter line's shard over them, whole.

**E107, a tile that waits for a GM** (the owner's ask of 13.11.2026): a GM's tile is no longer red under the glass; it
wears an action tile's look and the red-framed GM chip in its top right corner, as a Hope Call does. A pick row on the
GM's road carries the same chip; a Tier 0 item's Use wears it beside the flask; Legacy's cost stripes by kind.

**gaps-111, 1.2.105's known gaps** (the coordinator's list (a)-(g), and (h) on the owner's answer):
- **A late screen plays the sequence it missed** (the owner's "Przez 10 minut", Q-E61-1, Q-E94-4): a screen that loads
  within 10 minutes of a sequence's event - a player who joins late, a browser reloaded - plays the newest one it
  missed, once: the trial's entry, the verdict's cut-in or the start-of-day board. After 10 minutes, nothing. The
  end-of-day board is not played late.
- `game.drpg.a11y()` lists every disclosure, an action window's Details among them.
- Under the glass the sheet's and the strip's Hope and Action marks are E48 batch 5's diamond and dot.
- A focused panel wears the module's own focus ring in both themes.
- The GM handbooks' Hours and Colours paragraphs, EN and PL.
- A radio is round with its dot in the middle, a checkbox or a radio stands in the middle of its label's line, the
  Passages table's Polish Origin head reads "Źródło", a change of theme redraws a room's outline quietly, a season's
  last chapter names Season setup, a body announced during the Investigation's entry cuts its flashes.
- (c), the Event panel standing empty, was built and reverted: the owner keeps it showing only when there is an event.

**E104, the case planner plans every field** (the owner, 13.11.2026: "Od 1.2.112"): a planned Remnant holds every field
New Remnant asks, in its order (room, type, who left it, visibility, the tie, reinforced, name, words, analysis, the
GM's note, the picture), and Place hands them all on; a Key slot plans its visibility, who left it and its picture; a
**Planned Final Truth** and a **Planned Truth Bullet** (given by hand, with its recipient) are new kinds; the plans are
added from one select, so the Map keeps its height. A plan with no room (or a Truth Bullet with no name or recipient) is
named under the map's consistency check.

**E43, the second security round** (built; not marked shipped): `game.drpg.diagnoseSecrets()` and
`game.drpg.diagnoseTraps()` for a GM at the console; the voice plan grouped by where each account is sent; one registry
of the fields only the GMs hold (`SECRET_FIELDS`); a fuzz of every request from a player's console in scenario 30, and
in scenario 33 every request naming another player's character or a GM's road, sent from the wrong client; a
project's card opened while its project was unknown turns into it on discovery.

**E39 and E40's C1, tests** (built; not marked shipped): scenario 70 (movement end to end on the players' own pages),
scenario 99 (every row of `ACTIONS` driven from a player's page), tier 2 E35-T10 (every mode of the transfer policy)
and E39-T1 (a project entry's cases); E40-T1, a wrong verdict sentences the accused and the execution waits for the
trial's close. Tests only, no module code.

**Dash, the owner's bands** (the owner's decision of 13.11.2026, 8834a9b9): a successful Dash now gives 2, 3 or 4 free
crossings (12+, 18+, a critical), where it gave 1, 2 or 3; a miss still gives none. A crossing after the Free Move costs
one action and so does a Dash, so a success must beat a plain crossing. The player handbook's Dash table says the same.

**The owner's rule fixes of 13.11.2026** (a read of every action for one that another made pointless; the rel112-fix
line, 4ef5cceb, 73b6c5ba and feba55c3, merged in 909e0533):
- **Stashes: a roll to find, no roll to take.** A Search now draws from the room only; it never takes from somebody's
  stash, open or hidden, and its hidden-stash step of disadvantage is gone. A hidden stash is found only with Analyze's
  Find Stash (16+); after that you go through it like an open one: free, your pick, once per time of day.
- **The stash owner hears of it on walking in.** If somebody takes from your stash while you are away, you are told
  "somebody has been in your stash" the next time you enter that room - once, and never who or when. Nothing is said
  for anything taken while you stood in the room. The pending note is kept on the GM side and survives a reload.
- **Secure a Trace** leaves a Reinforced Remnant at the scene on every hit (it was the same as Leave a Clue, at a
  higher difficulty).
- **Relief's rest no longer offers Breath**: Relief costs 4 Hope and Breath gave 1 back. Breath is shown greyed with
  the reason, and refused on the GM's side too.
- **Texts**: free crossings from Sprint, Dash and Facilities are all called "a free crossing" (after a Dash the Move
  briefing said "the next room takes a Sprint"); the GM handbook says a Dynamic Action never stands in for looting.

## Before installing

- **New stored data**:
  - one world setting, `diceLookKind` (`dsn` or `daggerheart`, default `dsn`), beside the old `forceDiceLook`; a world
    from before reads its switch as it did (on is Dice So Nice's look, off each player's own), with no write and no
    migration. Both are held to a full Gamemaster's value: an Assistant GM's write is put back (E108).
  - the forced look now also writes the source GM's Dice So Nice `roleAppearance` on every user below full
    Gamemaster, and an actor's row in the GMs' look store gains `roles` (E108, Q-E108-2).
  - a stash's pending "somebody has been in your stash" note rides the GMs' existing rifle store (feba55c3): a row
    taken while the owner was away is marked, and the mark is cleared once the owner walks in and is told. Rows from
    before carry no mark, so nothing old is announced. A mark is lost if the thief's actor is deleted (the store
    prunes rows by thief).
  - at every death that is no Monocub's, a new character and its token in the world (E62 C3b): two new flags, the
    Spectator's `watcherOf` (once the death is public) and the token's `cubToken` (a Monocub's). **They are world data**:
    a player with the browser console can learn of a secret death from them before the body is found (the GM handbook
    says so).
- **The bridge**: a drawn roll's `roll.draw` may be asked again with `resend: true` once a GM is ready, and the
  primary GM answers it from its record (DH212b 4a). A browser on an older version never asks again.
- **No world migration**: no clause was added to `migrate.mjs`. Two language keys left: `DRPG.Action.gotIt` (Move's
  window, E100) and `DRPG.CaseMap.addIncident` (the planner's add buttons, E104).
- **Tile labels and words** change in both languages (E100's buttons, E101's window names, E108's choice); keys of
  settings are unchanged but the dice look's.

## Repository

- tools/stages.json: E108 added, planned for 1.2.112, touching sockets and rolls (9a735dd6), and shipped in the
  release commit.
- tools/tooltip-census.json and `node tools/check.mjs tooltips` (E102). The repository's instructions file lists
  `tooltips` beside `icons`, `glyphs` and `package`.

## Known gaps

- **E102 is not finished**: 54 rows "E102 C6" and 73 rows "E102 C12" in tools/tooltip-census.json are controls still to
  be given a tooltip or a reason; each goes red the day E102 is marked shipped. The census's guard against rows added by
  hand reads main's copy, which main does not have yet: it did not run.
- **E39, E40 and E43 are merged but not marked shipped**: E39's fourteen FLOWS rows name it as the stage that covers
  them; E40 has C2-C4 to come (1.2.114); E43's LIVE rows (a fuzz on a v14 sandbox, a bystander's Countdowns) are not
  yet items of audit/AUDIT-1.2.42.md 9.2, and its README chapter waits in docs/dev/e43/README-CHAPTER.md.
- **A Monocub's "Free" line** (E100) reads the character's next crossing price (`nextCrossingPrice`), which knows
  nothing of E72's rule that a Monocub's crossing is free; a Monocub whose Free Move flag is spent may read a price
  under its tiles while its crossing costs nothing. Read in source, not measured.
- **The dead's Spectator is world data** (above): a console learns of a secret death from it.
- **E103's order of Tamper and Direct Murder**, E107's chip, E108's three words and its basic dice under Daggerheart's
  look (Q-E108-1) are defaults, the owner to confirm.
- **600 ms** before "The GM is throwing your dice." is chosen, not measured (DH212b).
